title: A config file sandbox
description:
Run a config file written in Lua without letting it touch anything dangerous.

```
width = 800, title = "Xenon"
bad config: attempt to call a nil value (global 'os')... refused
```

starter.main.lua:
local good = [[
width = 800
height = width * 3 / 4
title = "Xenon"
]]

local function run_config(code)
  local env = {}
  return env
end

local settings = run_config(good)
print(settings.width, settings.title)

hints: `local chunk, err = load(code, "config", "t", env); if not chunk then return nil, err end; local ok, err2 = pcall(chunk)` (lesson 7.01).
Give `env` copies of only the functions you allow: `env.math = math` lets configs do sums but not reach `os`.
requirements: `load(code, "config", "t", env)` with an `env` table that holds only what configs may use (for example `math`).
The config's globals end up in `env`; read them from there.
A config that tries `os.exit()` or `io.open` fails safely.
stretch: Limit how long a config can run with `debug.sethook` and an instruction count.
